overview: This table holds the words shown on a character's command list, including the overview, passive skills, and attack explanations.
description: One row configures the text shown on a character's command-list page: the overview paragraph, up to four passive slots, and the name/description of the available normal, cursed-energy, super and character-specific extra attack widgets. Rows are selected indirectly from Character::Id_CommandList; name keys (and both parallel passive keys) also act as visibility switches when they are None. Text IDs are resolved through the localized CommandListTextDataTable shards.

Id.simple: The name that tells the game which character's command list these words belong to.
Id.technical: FName import key; the export writes it as `ID`, while the native member is `Id` in FGameDataTableRow_CommandList. AGameDataTableManager appends the loaded CommandListDataTable to CommandListDataTables, and BuildContents takes the first table whose FindRow<FGameDataTableRow_CommandList> matches Character::Id_CommandList. BuildContents stores CurrentCharacterId first, but returns before populating the listed text/action widgets when Id_CommandList is None or no matching row exists.

Id_CommandListText_CharacterDescription.simple: The paragraph shown at the top of the character's command list.
Id_CommandListText_CharacterDescription.technical: FName passed directly to CharacterExplanation->SetTextIdOnly; the text request resolves it in the current language through GameTextManager. This path has no explicit None check (a None key would simply resolve to empty text), and all exported rows supply a key of the form CMD_CHARACTER_DESCRIPTION_CP_*.

Id_CommandListText_PassiveName.simple: The names shown for up to four passive skills, in display order. Leave one empty to hide that skill.
Id_CommandListText_PassiveName.technical: TArray<FName>, read by zero-based index in the order of the four passive widget slots constructed in InitializeWidget (Passive_1..4). When both parallel arrays contain the index and neither value is None, the name is added as the SKILL_NAME text parameter of SYS_COMMANDLIST_LABEL_0002 for PassiveName; otherwise the slot stays hidden. Every exported row supplies four entries, with None used for unused slots.

Id_CommandListText_PassiveDescription.simple: The explanations for the character's passive skills, in the same order. A passive appears when both its name and explanation are filled in.
Id_CommandListText_PassiveDescription.technical: TArray<FName> parallel to Id_CommandListText_PassiveName, read by the same zero-based widget-slot index and passed directly to PassiveExplanation->SetTextIdOnly. A slot is shown only when both arrays contain that index and neither the name nor the description is None. Every exported row supplies four entries; None marks unused slots.

Id_CommandListText_NormalAttack_1_Name.simple: The name shown for the character's first normal attack. Leave it empty to hide that attack from the command list.
Id_CommandListText_NormalAttack_1_Name.technical: FName copied into FGameCommandListActionParameter::NameTextId and set on the attack widget's AttackName with SetTextIdOnly. UGameCommandListWidget::BuildContents calls SetShow(!IsNone()) on this widget, so a None name hides it. All 27 exported rows have a non-None key in this field.

Id_CommandListText_NormalAttack_1_Descri.simple: The explanation shown under the first normal attack. The attack appears when its name is filled in.
Id_CommandListText_NormalAttack_1_Descri.technical: FName copied into FGameCommandListActionParameter::DescriptionTextId. UGameCommandListActionWidget resolves it with GameTextManager and parses `<SplitCommand>` sections, bracketed labels and level markers into the explanation rows. Visibility is controlled by the paired Name key, not by this description.

CommandListAttackPropertyType_NormalAtta.simple: These saved attack details describe the first normal attack. All current data leaves them empty, and their effect is unclear.
CommandListAttackPropertyType_NormalAtta.technical: TArray<EGameCommandListAttackPropertyType> (uint8 UENUM with None, DirectAttack, Shooting, Buff, Debuff, Heal, Trap, Special, DomainExpansion and Invalid=255). Every exported row serializes three EGameCommandListAttackPropertyType::None entries. No C++ reader for this member was found in the available Source. BuildContents never populates PropertyIconResources (it explicitly assigns an empty array for cursed-energy attack 1 and extra attack 1; the other parameters keep the default empty array), so UGameCommandListActionWidget collapses all three property icons in this path. The three serialized slots do not prove an icon mapping.

Id_CommandListText_TagComboAttack_Name.technical: FName serialized in every exported row (keys of the form CMD_COMMAND_NAME_CP_*_7000) and present in all exported locale shards, but no C++ reader for this member was found in the available Source. UGameCommandListWidget::BuildContents never references it, so no visibility, text-slot or other runtime behavior can be asserted from traced code.

notes: The export contains 27 unique rows and one field-level runtime consumer path: UGameCommandListWidget::BuildContents, which forwards text IDs to UGameCommandListActionWidget and UGameCommandListPassiveWidget. AGameDataTableManager only loads/caches the UDataTable into CommandListDataTables; BuildContents scans that array and uses the first row matching Character::Id_CommandList. In the export, every command row is referenced, while 17 of 48 Character rows have Id_CommandList=None and get no content from this path.

Attack name keys control widget visibility via SetShow(!IsNone()); passive slots require both parallel arrays to have valid, non-None entries. Every attack name/description except ExtraAttack_1/2 is non-None in all 27 rows; ExtraAttack_1 is non-None only for CP_050 and ExtraAttack_2 only for CP_170. The character-description and TagCombo keys are non-None in every row, but only the former is read in the traced C++ path.

Serialized values are not native defaults: the reconstructed row struct has no member initializers and an empty constructor, which would leave FName values as None and TArray values empty. The export instead writes four passive entries per row and three property-enum entries per attack (all EGameCommandListAttackPropertyType::None). The 11 property arrays and the TagCombo key have no found C++ consumer; property icons are collapsed because BuildContents never supplies PropertyIconResources.

Description IDs are resolved through GameTextManager using locale-specific CommandListTextDataTable_<language> tables; all 628 non-None keys used by this table exist in all 11 exported locale shards. Command-button labels, category colors, character name/image/gauges, attack-set IDs and energy type come from static widget maps and Character/CharacterUI/CharacterImage/CharacterBaseParameter/CharacterCursedEnergy/Action rows, not from this table; the widget also has hard-coded CP_-specific overrides.

Row values come from a shipped-table data export. Runtime behavior is traced through reconstructed C++ annotated with retail RVAs, not observed in a retail runtime; no Blueprint behavior is assumed, and additional editor-only or unexported shards cannot be ruled out.

usages.detail: After all primary-asset DataTable loads complete, resolves CommandListDataTable and appends the non-null UDataTable to the CommandListDataTables member array cached on the manager.

Searches the manager's CommandListDataTables array in order and uses the first row named by the selected character's Id_CommandList; a None ID or missing row returns before the content below is built.
Sets the character overview text from the row's character-description key.
Iterates the passive widget slots, reads aligned name/description arrays, and shows only slots where both keys are present and not None; the name is passed as a SKILL_NAME text parameter.
Builds each normal-attack action widget from the paired name/description keys, sets its category color and command label from widget-local data, and hides it when the name is None.
Builds cursed-energy attack widgets from their name/description keys plus Action-table attack sets and UI energy type.
Builds the super-cursed-energy widget from its name/description keys.
Shows the CP_050 and CP_170 extra-attack widgets only when their respective name keys are not None.
OpenForCharacter and the previous/next-character handlers call BuildContents, so each opening or character change repeats the CommandListDataTable row lookup.
Indirect text consumer: SetupContent sets AttackName from NameTextId, then resolves DescriptionTextId through GameTextManager and splits `<SplitCommand>` sections into the explanation/level rows.
Loads CommandListTextDataTable_<language> with the other localized text tables, which is how the FName keys stored in this table become localized strings.
